mergedParams.userDescription: Smooth horizontal slide, text gliding into frame with perfect easing. typo kinetics for titles/captions/other text..

output.title: Smooth Horizontal Text Slide with Easing Animation

prompts.prompt: Create a smooth horizontal sliding text animation preset that mimics professional video title sequences. The text should glide into frame from the right side with a silk-smooth ease-out curve, as if being gently pushed by an invisible force that gradually releases. Think of it like a camera dolly move in reverse - the text moves while the viewport stays static. The animation should feel premium and refined, like opening credits in a high-end documentary. Each word should have a subtle staggered delay creating a cascading effect, where words arrive in sequence but overlap slightly in their motion. The text should decelerate naturally as it reaches its final position, with the last 20% of the animation being almost imperceptible movement for that perfect settling feeling.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'overflow-hidden w-full h-full relative' for the container. Create a TextAtom for each word from caption data, wrapped in BaseLayout components with 'inline-block' positioning. Apply translateX effect starting from 120% (off-screen right) to 0% with ease-out easing over 0.8-1.2 seconds relative timing. Stagger each word's start time by 0.05-0.08 seconds using the word's index. Add a subtle opacity fade from 0 to 1 during the first 30% of the slide animation. Use 'will-change-transform' on moving elements and ensure GPU acceleration with 'transform-gpu'. Consider adding a very slight blur effect (0.5px to 0px) during movement for motion blur simulation. Structure as reusable internal effect preset 'smooth-slide-in' that can accept direction and timing parameters.

prompts.prompt: Design a kinetic typography preset where text slides horizontally with momentum-based physics, as if each word has weight and mass. Imagine editing a fast-paced commercial where text needs to grab attention immediately. The slide should start explosively fast and then ease into position with a slight overshoot and settle-back, like a spring dampening system. This creates dynamic energy perfect for action-oriented content or energetic brand messaging. Layer in a subtle scale animation (0.95 to 1.0) during the slide to add dimensionality. The text should feel like it's being magnetically pulled into its final position with just a tiny bounce at the end.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Implement using BaseLayout with 'flex items-center justify-start gap-2' for word spacing. Each TextAtom should be wrapped in a BaseLayout with individual effects arrays. Use a custom spring easing function or approximate with cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55) for overshoot effect. Apply translateX from -100vw to final position with a 0.6 second duration. Add a secondary translateX keyframe at 85% progress that goes 5% past the final position, then settles back. Include scaleX and scaleY effects from 0.95 to 1.0 synchronized with the slide. Use 'transform-style-preserve-3d' for better rendering. Consider fitDurationTo: 'children' to ensure all words complete their animations. Add 'transition-transform' as a fallback for reduced motion preferences.

prompts.prompt: Build a cinematic text reveal where words slide in horizontally while simultaneously emerging from a soft gaussian blur, creating a focus-pull effect similar to rack focusing in cinematography. The text should feel like it's sliding along an invisible track while a camera operator adjusts focus to bring it into sharp clarity. This dual animation creates depth and sophistication perfect for documentary titles or elegant brand presentations. The blur should be heaviest at the start of the slide and completely clear by the 60% mark, allowing viewers to read the text before it fully settles into position.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using 'relative w-full h-full' as container. Apply a combination of translateX (from 150% to 0%) and blur filter effects (from 8px to 0px) on TextAtom components. Use different timing functions: ease-out for translation, ease-in-out for blur. Set blur to reach 0 at 60% of animation duration while translate continues to 100%. Add 'backdrop-blur-none' to parent and use CSS filter for blur effect. Include slight opacity animation (0.7 to 1) for additional depth. Ensure GPU acceleration with 'transform-gpu' and 'will-change-filter will-change-transform'. Create as a composed preset using sub-preset dependencies for blur and slide effects separately, allowing independent timing control.

prompts.prompt: Develop a typewriter-meets-slide animation where text appears to be typed out character by character, but each complete word slides smoothly into its final position from the right. Think of it as combining the classic typewriter effect with modern kinetic movement - perfect for tech presentations or coding tutorials. As each word completes typing, it should glide leftward to make room for the next word, creating a continuous flow of revealing and positioning. The slide motion should be quick and snappy (0.2-0.3 seconds) with a strong ease-out curve, while the typing effect provides the primary timing rhythm.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'flex flex-wrap items-baseline' for word flow. Implement word-by-word reveal using caption data timing. For each word, use a TextAtom with clipPath animation (inset from right) for typewriter effect over word.duration. Once revealed, trigger translateX animation from current position to final position using negative margins or transform. Calculate final positions based on cumulative word widths. Use 'inline-flex' for each word container to maintain proper spacing. Add 'font-mono' for authentic typewriter aesthetic. Consider using internal effect preset for the slide motion that triggers at word.endTime. Implement with requestAnimationFrame for smooth character reveal timing if needed.

prompts.prompt: Create a liquid slide animation where text flows into frame like water finding its level. The horizontal movement should have a fluid, almost viscous quality with multiple ease points creating an organic S-curve motion path. Imagine pouring honey - fast at first, then slowing with natural deceleration. Add subtle vertical oscillation (like a wave) during the horizontal slide to enhance the liquid feeling. This works beautifully for organic brands, nature documentaries, or any content requiring smooth, natural motion. The text should feel alive and flowing rather than mechanically animated.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Build with BaseLayout using 'relative overflow-visible' to allow for oscillation outside bounds. Apply complex keyframe animation with multiple points: translateX at 0% (200%), 20% (100%), 50% (20%), 80% (5%), 100% (0%). Add synchronized translateY oscillation: 0% (0), 25% (-3%), 50% (2%), 75% (-1%), 100% (0). Use cubic-bezier(0.45, 0.05, 0.55, 0.95) for smooth S-curve. Duration of 1.2-1.5 seconds for fluid feel. Apply these as generic effects with AnimationRange arrays. Consider adding slight rotation (-1 to 1 degree) during motion for additional fluidity. Use 'subpixel-antialiased' for smooth rendering during sub-pixel movements.

prompts.prompt: Design a parallax-inspired sliding text system where different text elements (main title, subtitle, caption) slide in from the same direction but at different speeds and distances, creating depth layers like in video compositing. The main title moves the furthest and fastest, subtitle moves medium distance/speed, and captions move least distance/slowest. This creates a pseudo-3D effect perfect for cinematic titles or layered information hierarchy. Each layer should have slightly different easing to enhance the depth perception - faster layers use aggressive ease-out, slower layers use gentler easing.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with nested BaseLayout components, each with z-index layering (z-10, z-20, z-30). Main title: translateX from 200% to 0% over 0.8s with ease-out. Subtitle: translateX from 150% to 0% over 1.0s with cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94). Caption: translateX from 100% to 0% over 1.2s with ease-in-out. Use 'absolute inset-0' positioning for each layer with specific top/bottom adjustments. Add slight scale differences (1.0 for front, 0.95 for middle, 0.9 for back) to enhance depth. Include opacity gradients (1.0, 0.9, 0.8) for atmospheric perspective. Consider using childrenProps for applying layer-specific classes and repeatChildrenProps for consistent spacing within layers.

prompts.prompt: Build a staggered cascade slide where text breaks into individual characters that slide in with precise choreography, like dominoes falling in reverse. Each character starts its slide slightly after the previous one, creating a wave-like motion across the text. The timing should follow a acceleration curve - first characters move slowly, middle characters faster, last characters fastest, creating urgency and momentum. Perfect for sports graphics, action titles, or any content needing dramatic buildup. Add micro-rotations to each character during slide for additional dynamism.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Split text into individual characters using TextAtom with 'inline-block' for each. Calculate stagger delay using exponential function: delay = baseDelay * Math.pow(0.9, index). Base delay of 0.05s, total animation 0.4s per character. Apply translateX from 50px to 0px with strong ease-out. Add rotation from 5deg to 0deg synchronized with slide. Use 'transform-origin-center' for rotation pivot. Implement with CSS custom properties for dynamic timing calculations. Consider performance with will-change on all moving elements but remove after animation completes. Use BaseLayout with 'flex flex-wrap' for character container. Create as internal effect preset 'cascade-slide' with configurable acceleration curve.

prompts.prompt: Develop an elastic slide preset where text stretches horizontally as it moves, like pulling taffy. The text begins compressed (scaleX: 0.3), slides in while expanding to slightly over-scale (scaleX: 1.1), then snaps back to normal (scaleX: 1.0). This creates a playful, energetic effect perfect for youth-oriented content, gaming graphics, or fun brand animations. The stretch should be most extreme during the fastest part of the slide (middle 40-60% of animation), creating a speed-blur effect. Add subtle skewX during the stretch phase to enhance the motion dynamics.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with TextAtom components. Apply three synchronized effects: translateX (-100% to 0%), scaleX with keyframes (0%: 0.3, 30%: 0.7, 50%: 1.15, 70%: 1.05, 100%: 1.0), skewX (0%: 0deg, 40%: -8deg, 60%: 3deg, 100%: 0deg). Duration of 0.6-0.8s with custom cubic-bezier for bounce. Use 'transform-origin-left' for scale/skew to maintain left edge anchor during slide. Add 'font-stretch' CSS property animation from condensed to normal for additional stretch effect if font supports it. Implement as generic effects with AnimationRange arrays. Consider adding motion blur using filter: blur during peak velocity (40-60% progress).

prompts.prompt: Create a reveal-through-mask slide where text appears to slide behind an invisible viewport window, similar to a film strip moving through a projector gate. The text itself doesn't change opacity - it's simply revealed/hidden by the sliding motion through a defined rectangular area. This technique is perfect for news tickers, scrolling credits, or any situation where text needs to maintain consistent appearance while moving through frame. Add subtle ease-in acceleration at start and ease-out deceleration at end for professional polish.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Implement with BaseLayout using 'overflow-hidden' as the mask container with defined width/height via 'w-96 h-16' or dynamic sizing. Inner TextAtom positioned absolutely with whitespace-nowrap. Apply translateX animation from calc(100% + element width) to negative element width for complete pass-through. Use 'ease-in-out' timing over 3-4 seconds for smooth ticker effect. For partial reveals, use clipPath with inset values animated in sync with translate. Add 'pointer-events-none' during animation, 'pointer-events-auto' when stopped. Consider implementing loop property for continuous scrolling. Use fitDurationTo: 'scene' to adapt speed to scene duration. Create variants for different reveal directions using rotation transforms on the container.

prompts.prompt: Design a momentum-transfer slide where each word appears to push the next word into position, like Newton's cradle or billiard balls. The first word slides in fast, 'hits' its position, and transfers its energy to make the second word start sliding, creating a chain reaction. This creates engaging cause-and-effect motion perfect for sequential information reveal, step-by-step tutorials, or connected narrative text. Each word should have a tiny recoil bounce when 'hit' by the previous word, adding physical realism to the animation.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using 'flex items-center gap-0' initially, expanding gap as words settle. Each word is a TextAtom in its own BaseLayout wrapper. First word: translateX from -100% to final position over 0.4s. On 80% completion, trigger next word's animation. Each subsequent word starts from translateX: 20px (pushed position) to 0px (settled) over 0.3s with overshoot easing. Add micro-animation on 'impact': scaleX 1.0 to 0.95 to 1.0 over 0.1s. Use event emitters or calculated delays based on word index and timing. Implement 'will-change-transform' just before each word's animation starts. Consider using audio impact sounds synchronized with each word's landing via AudioAtom with specific timestamps.
